recognize_zh: 紅箭頭所指細胞大小與嗜中性球相近，細胞質布滿粗大、深紫色的嗜鹼性顆粒並覆蓋於核上，使核形不清，即嗜鹼性球（basophil）；左側為分葉核嗜中性球可作對照。
features: Cell (arrow) similar in size to a neutrophil with coarse, dark purple basophilic granules
Granules densely overlie and partially obscure the nucleus, so lobation is not clearly visible
Small paler cytoplasmic area at one pole with fewer granules
Adjacent segmented neutrophil with fine pale granules for comparison
Normochromic red cells with scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normochromic red cells, scattered platelets, and a segmented neutrophil. The indicated cell is of similar size and contains numerous coarse, dark purple cytoplasmic granules that overlie and partially obscure the nucleus, consistent with a basophil. No blasts or immature granulocytes are seen in this field. In a patient with chronic myeloid leukemia, basophilia is a characteristic finding, and a basophil count ≥20% is a WHO-HAEM4 accelerated-phase criterion.

ddx.vs: Mast cells are larger with a round central nucleus and uniformly packed granules and are rarely seen in blood.
Toxic neutrophils have a clearly visible segmented nucleus with finer dark granules not obscuring it.
Eosinophils contain larger refractile orange-red granules with a bilobed nucleus clearly visible.
An immature basophil has a round, non-segmented nucleus with finer chromatin, whereas a mature basophil has a lobated nucleus.
